chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: The big band breaks up: package tours and the rise of rock
summary: Tate recalls the first Basie band breaking up, and says agents' bird-group packages and rock killed the big bands.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Were you in the band when Wardell Gray was --
No, Wardell replaced me. See, the band broke up.

And actually, the big band, I stayed with until, you know, the first band broke up. So they disbanded for a while. I'll tell you what happened to me. I started to tell you yesterday. Well, see, I'd never been around New York anytime except to come and play with Basie, because our band was a traveling band. So I go down to Local 802 to put my transfer card in and I see Lucky Millinder down there. Lucky had a good band. And Lucky says, "Hey, what are you doing?" I said, "I'm just putting a transfer in." He says, "I understand the band's breaking up." He says, "Man, what the hell's wrong?" He says, "That's the best band he ever had." I said, "Well, I don't know. We weren't making any money, you know, out on the road," because they were sending those bird groups out -- we called them "bird groups," you know.

And they would send out big packages like maybe about seven of them and each one of them had a hit record. See what I mean? Now, promoters have to do that and agents and things, they have killed the big bands, when you really think of it

in that respect because -- but for them, they were getting like seven and eight commissions, where they would only get one like with Basie. And the things -- people were at a standstill, at a turnaround, beboppers coming in. They didn't know what to accept and they started -- and they didn't have a beat and kids wanted to dance and with the rock, they were getting a beat, you know, like what they wanted to hear. And it was just too much for a band like Basie's.
